drafts.angle: Cost-per-task math (rides @gregisenberg's 'about the same as Opus 5.5… half the cost per task', 43K, and the Gemini 4 Neon launch at 981K)
drafts.draft_en:
Everyone's comparing models on cost per task.

Nobody's pricing the most expensive task in marketing:

the ad that ships with a claim legal never approved.

Cheapest model in the stack is the one that checks the output before it goes live.
drafts.video_tip: 15s vertical: on-screen ticker of 'cost per task' numbers for generation, then a hard cut to a real Aubric check flagging an unapproved claim (block). End on the last line. Burn in captions; use only your own ads and real product footage.

drafts.angle: Tiny follow-up post (rides @OfficialLoganK's 'Neon is a great model : )', 411K, after the main launch)
drafts.draft_en:
New models every week now.

Same brand rules every week.

That's the whole case for a verifier : )
drafts.video_tip: 6s loop: model names flicking past fast (generic labels, no third-party logos), then a static card with your brand-rules checklist and an 'APPROVED' stamp from a real Aubric run. Text overlay is the post.

drafts.angle: Mechanism how-to that earns saves (rides @gregisenberg's 'top 1% AI agent content team', 1.4K bookmarks, and @levie's 'agents that you orchestrate', 39K)
drafts.draft_en:
How to let AI agents make your ads without waking up to a legal problem:

1. Write brand rules as code, not a PDF
2. Load the claims legal actually approved
3. Add each ad platform's policy
4. Put a verifier between the agent and publish: approve / fix / block
5. Keep the trace for every ad

Orchestrate the agents. Verify the output.
drafts.video_tip: 25s screen-record: numbers 1-5 stack on screen one beat at a time; on step 4 show a real Aubric approve / fix / block result, on 5 the trace view. Hold the last line 2s.
